replies.content: @hacdias "Because MD5 is a relatively weak algorithm, it is possible to create deliberate hash "collisions". That is, take some data and manipulate it until it has the same MD5 as a different piece of data."This is confusing collision attacks and second preimage attacks.MD5 and SHA-1 are broken in collisions. IE, two inputs collide to an *unknown* output.Both are secure against second preimages. IE, you have an input w/ hash and look for another input it collides with.
